steps.text: Stir together milk, sugar, tapioca, and beaten eggs in a slow cooker until well combined.
Cook on Low for 6 hours or High for 3 hours, stirring occasionally. Serve warm.

raw_recipe.headline: Slow Cooker Tapioca Pudding
raw_recipe.description: This creamy and comforting tapioca pudding is made in the slow cooker with milk, sugar, small pearl tapioca, and eggs for a no-fuss, make-ahead dessert.
raw_recipe.name: Slow Cooker Tapioca Pudding

review.reviewBody:
I love Tapioca Pudding, but, I don't make it very often as it does take watching over. I am glad to say that is not the case anymore. I will make this pudding-doubled-alot from now on. 
Easy to do, just measure and put it in crockpot. I took some other reviewers advice and added some vanilla and salt, doubled the recipe and cooked it on high for 3 hrs. Came out perfecto.
My only advice would be to break up the eggs, prior to putting in crockpot, don't just drop them in there and then wonder why it doesn't come out right. You need to break them up. Also, be sure to stir during cooking, it helps to keep everything mixed up. So, that you don't end up with layers of eggs, tapioca, etc.
Otherwise--just enjoy eating this comfort food.

After reading ALL the reviews, I have successfully tried making this 2 times. Here is how I did it twice with great results BOTH times.

4C Milk(used 1%) 1/2 C Sugar Put in blender for 4 sec. Added 2 eggs and Pinch of salt. Again blended 4 secs. Pour into my Old Rival Crock pot. Stir in 1/2 C small pearl tapioca(bought at Amish store here).

Put on lid,turn on High. Every 15min, I gave it a quick wisk, hitting the sides and bottom. This was done in 2 hrs. Add 1 tsp Vanilla pour in serving dishes, chill. 
Second time I got interrupted after an hour, put temp down to low the second hour, still made sure I gave it a quick wisk every 20 min. It was still done in 2hrs!!. 
I feel you still have to stir this often to make it come out right. You are just not standing over it like when on the stove. Passing this along to several friends.

After reading some reviews, I did change it slightly.Use ONLY SMALL PEARL tapioca. I beat 2 eggs well,not slightly beaten, but not to foamy stage. The first time, iI used almond coconut milk, the second time I used regular milk and added a 1/2 tsp vanilla, for variety. I will use the same amt of vanilla in either milk in the future. I reduced the sugar to 1/2 C. Actually, 1/4 C sugar , 1/4 C local honey. I mixed the beaten eggs in with the milk when adding to crock pot , then dumped in the rest of the ingredients. My pot doesn't have medium, only warm, so I cooked it on warm for 3 hours, stirring , not whisking, with a French whisk about every 20 minutes timer was set, it’s easy to forget the dish, for the duration. It was wonderful!

I would argue the failures are from 'low' settings (on the pot) that run too hot. After my first failure, I came up with this 2 hour recipe, adding the milk and egg at the end, like my mom. 2-3 servings Ingredients 1/2 cup milk 1 cup water 1/3 cup white sugar (2 pk sweetener) 1/2 cup pearl tapioca 1 egg, lightly beaten 1/2 tsp vanilla pinch salt Combine tapioca, water, salt Cook on low 1hr 45 min Stir and add more water to consistency (check every 15-20 min) Stir together milk, sweetener, vanilla & egg Stir above into tapioca, continue to cook 15 min (or more) Cool in fridge 3-4 hrs to thicken

While this is an easy recipe, it can also be tricky. First, I think it is essential to add some flavoring to this dish. I add a teaspoon of Mexican vanilla extract during the last half hour of cooking. Also, for those having trouble with the egg part of this dish, tempering is the answer. One hour before your pudding is done, whisk your eggs in a medium bowl, then slowly add a bit of the hot tapioca mixture to the eggs, stirring constantly. Go SLOW. Keep stirring and adding more of the hot mixture to the eggs until they are quite warm, then add to the crock pot and stir thoroughly. Stir again 30 minutes later (and add the vanilla extract). Cook another 30 minutes or so, and voila - delicious tapioca pudding, perfectly cooked!

This was absolutely delicious. It was easy and much better than standing over a stove for 30 minutes stirring. I did soak my small pearls over night in some of the milk. I started the slow cooker on high for 45 minutes then turned down to low. Total time was 1.5 hours. As others recommend I did add a little salt and vanilla. I tempered the eggs and added in the last 1/2 and turned off and added the vanilla. I did not use any regular sugar instead I used organic Stevia and only 1 tsp. and 2% milk both made no difference to the consistency of the pudding. I made 12 servings. This was fabulous!

I made it the first time according to the recipe: 4 stars. The following changes made it 5:

I used 1/4 c white sugar and 1/4 c brown. Be sure to whisk everything well. I stirred every 15 minutes with my whisk. (Which didn't get the entire bottom edge of the crock pot and that burned so next time I'll use a utensil that can get that!) I added 1tsp vanilla about 1/2 hour before it was done. It was pretty soft even after shutting the crock pot off and letting it sit. But after overnight in the fridge? Completely set and I could hold a spoonful upside down without it falling out! Awesome!

WORKS BEAUTIFULLY EVERY TIME! I love this recipe! So much less intense on my shoulder than traditional double boiler method that requires constant stirring. 

If using large pearl tapioca soaking overnight is a must for this to turn out right!

This is a super easy recipe, a few other reviewers mentioned adding in Vanilla extract I totally concur. I add about 2tsp-1Tbsp depending on size of batch (I usually make a double batch). Prior to adding to heat: Also would like to recommend beating eggs well in a separate bowl first, then adding to the milk and beating again until well blended while all are cold help to reduce egg separating later. Then I like to add the sugar and beat a 3rd time to ensure sugar dissolves. Then I just let it cook in crockpot and add the Vanilla extract just before placing in serving dish and cooling in fridge.

I used tiny pearl tapioca from my local Asian store and that worked perfectly. I also added 1 teasp. vanilla and reduced the sugar to 1/2 cup; (this reduced the calories per serving to 170). When I make it next time I may try adding an additional egg for richness or using half and half because the current recipe is a little "light", which is fine for me, but not the hubster. Also, depending on your crock pot, I would suggest starting out on low for the 1st hour rather than starting out on medium or high. If the milk gets too hot too fast the egg will cook and the result will look like scrambled eggs. I cooked it on low first and then switched to high (I don't have a medium setting) and it's magic!

I just made this and it turned out perfectly. I doubled the recipe, used heavy whipping cream, evaporated milk & water b/c that's what I had on hand. I also added 2 Tbsp of vanilla & 1 Tbsp of cinnamon to spice it up for Thanksgiving. I blended the ingredients very well except for the tapioca before adding to the crockpot to make sure there was no curdling. I stirred it with a wisk every 30 minutes to make sure it didn't clump too. I cooked it on high for about 2.5 hrs and it could not have turned out more perfectly. Thank you for sharing.

I make this recipe all the time, exactly as written, but I use large pearl tapioca. I always double the recipe and stir with a whisk 4 or 5 times while it is cooking. I start cooking it on high for an hour, then continue on medium for 2 hours, or until it has thickened and the eggs are set. It thickens as it cools. All crock pots cook at different temperatures, so you might have to adjust the time. My last crock pot cooked a double batch in 4 hours.
Made as stated, added a pinch of salt and stirred every 30 minutes. Once cooked, stirred in 1 tsp vanilla. Sprinkled cinnamon on top before serving.
Mine looks like the eggs have cooked and separated slightly? I followed the instructions and it tastes great but doesn’t have that wonderful creamy texture to it.
I added vanilla (didn't measure) midway and again within the last half hour. Delish and easy!
Add eggs and 1 tsp vanilla at the end. Cook less for instant tapioca, 3 to 4 hrs on low.
Easy to make, Family loved it! Even though it is not the best it is still good. I make it often!
Perfect tapioca made in my insta pot on slow cooker mode, added my homemade vanilla extract and a pinch of salt. Will probably make this every week lol
Gr8 recipe, added vanilla and almond extracts. This way gives me time to do others things, by not having to constantly watch.
